overview.text: The Rubber Boa is a small, gentle boa of western North America. It is the most northerly boa in the world, and its loose, shiny skin makes it look and feel like rubber.

identification.text: Small, smooth and shiny with loose, wrinkly skin. Usually plain tan to dark brown with a lighter belly, sometimes olive-green, yellow or orange.

size.label: Adults
size.text: 38 to 84 cm long; newborns are 19 to 23 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Western North America: southern British Columbia south to central California, and east to western Montana, Wyoming and Utah.

habitat.text: Grassland, meadows, chaparral, forests and high mountains, from sea level to over 3,000 m. It cannot stand heat and dryness but copes with surprisingly cold places.

behaviour.text: Mainly active at night and at dusk. It is one of the calmest snakes and very rarely bites; if threatened it gives off a smelly musk.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young - usually 1 to 5, at most about 9 - and females do not breed every year.

funfacts.text: It lives farther north than any other boa in the world.

recognise.text: Looks like rubber: smooth, shiny, loose skin.
Plain tan to brown, with a lighter belly.
